sentences.text: Adimulam Vajramma vs Kotte Kumar, on 8 November, 2024

The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty
 M.A.C.M.A.No.1934 of 2014
Judgment:

Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded in the judgment and decree, dated 13.02.2014 passed in M.V.O.P.No.87 of 2013 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Karimnagar (for short "the Tribunal"), the appellants/claimants preferred the present appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Karimnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For convenience, hereinafter, the parties are referred to as they are arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that on 02.12.2012, one Adimulam Laxminarayana (hereinafter referred to as 'the deceased') was crossing the road, one RTC bus bearing No.AP 29 Z 590 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed the deceased.
Immediately, the deceased was shifted to Lifeline Hospital at Karimnagar.
However, the deceased succumbed to the injuries while he was taking to Hyderabad for better treatment.

The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.28,70,000/- for the death of the deceased i.e., one Adimulam Laxminarayana, husband of claimant LNA, J Macma_1934_2014 No.1, father of claimant No.2 and son of claimant No.3, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 02.12.2012.

According to the claimants, the deceased was aged 55 years and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month by running Sapthagiri Auto Oil Store, Karimnagar and used to contribute his entire earnings for the welfare of the family
. Due to his sudden demise, the claimants lost their bread winner, love and affection.
Therefore, they filed the claim petition against the respondent Nos.1 and 2 claiming compensation of Rs.28,70,000/- towards compensation under different heads.
4. Before the Tribunal, the respondent Nos.1 and 2, filed counters denying the manner in which the accident took place, including the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
It is also stated that the quantum of compensation claimed was excessive, baseless and prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
1. Whether the pleaded accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the RTC bus bearing No.AP 29 Z 590 by the respondent No.1?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what amount and from which of the respondents?
3.
To what relief?

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to prove their case, PWs.1 to 3 were examined and Exs
.A1 to A12 and Exs.X1 to X4 were marked.
On behalf of the respondents, RW.1 was examined and no documents were marked.

7. Considering the pleadings and oral, documentary evidence available on record, the Tribunal held that the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the APSRTC Bus by its driver and accordingly,
awarded an amount of Rs.10,15,000/- with interest at 7.5% per annum payable by respondent Nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally.
Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation, the claimants filed the present appeal.
8. Heard Sri A.Kesava Reddy, learned counsel for the appellants/claimants and Sri N.Vasudeva Reddy, learned Standing Counsel for RTC.
Perused the record.

9. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants contended that the claimants have established that the deceased was earning Rs.30,000/- per month as proprietor, Sapthagiri Auto Oil Store,
Karimnagar, but the Tribunal has erroneously took the income of the deceased as Rs.10,000/- per month, which is a meager amount.
Hence, he prayed the Court to enhance the compensation.
On the other hand, the learned Standing Counsel for the RTC, has contended that the learned Tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation and the same needs no interference by this Court.
11. The finding of the Tribunal with regard to the manner in which the accident took place has become final as the same is not challenged by either of the respondents.

Consideration:
12. As per the income tax returns filed by the deceased, his date of birth is shown as 06.07.1950 and considering the same, the Tribunal has rightly taken the age of the deceased as 62 years.
13.

Insofar as the future prospects is concerned, as per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others 1, since the age of the deceased was taken as 62 years, no additional income of the actual salary of the deceased can be added towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As far as the multiplier is concerned, as per paragraph- 42 of the said decision, the multiplier is '7' for the age groups of 61 to 65 and the Tribunal rightly applied the multiplier '7'.
The other contention of the learned counsel for the claimants is that Tribunal erred in taking the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/-.

Insofar as the income of the deceased is concerned,
the claimants have placed Exs.A9 to A12 and Ex
.X1 to X4 to support that the deceased was earning Rs.30,000/- per month as proprietor of Sapthagiri Auto Oil Store, Karimnagar.

Therefore,
considering the age and avocation of the deceased, this Court is inclined to fix the income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month.

2 15.

The other contention raised by the learned counsel for the claimants with regard to living expenses of the deceased, as the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma (Smt) and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another 2, the Hon'ble Apex Court at paragraph-30 held that where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one-third (1/3th), where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3.

entities.text: Sarla Verma (Smt) and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants in the present claim are 3, therefore, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
(2009) 6 SCC 121 LNA, J Macma_1934_2014 Conclusion:

16. In view of the above discussion, after deducting 1/3rd therefrom towards his personal and living expenses, the contribution of income by the deceased to the family comes to Rs.10,000/- per month (Rs.15,000-(Rs.15,000 x 1/3)).

Since the age of the deceased was 62 years as held by the Tribunal based on his date of birth in income tax returns, the appropriate multiplier is '7' as per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma (supra).
Adopting multiplier '7', the total loss of dependency comes to Rs.8,40,000/- (Rs.10,000/- x 12 x 7).

17. At this juncture, it is pertinent to note that though the learned counsel for the claimants raised contention that the Tribunal has deducted 1/3rd towards personal expenses of the deceased, a perusal of the record would disclose that the Tribunal has taken monthly income of the deceased as Rs.10,000/- and directly calculated the total loss of dependency without deducting any amount towards personal expenses of the deceased.

As such, the total loss of dependency arrived by the Tribunal i.e., Rs.8,40,000/- (Rs.10,000/- x 12 x 7) and this Court i.e., Rs.8,40,000/-
[((Rs.15,000x1/3) - Rs.15,000) x 12 x 7) is one and the same, which is reasonable and the same needs no interference by this Court.

Further, the Tribunal has rightly awarded LNA, J Macma_1934_2014 Rs.25,000/- each to claimant Nos.2 and 3 towards loss of love and affection;
Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of consortium to claimant No.1 and Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expenses and the same needs no interference by this Court.

entities.text: LNA, J Macma_1934_2014 Rs.25,000/- each to
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
Thus, in all, the claimants are entitled to Rs.10,15,000/-.
18.
Accordingly, the M.A.C.M.A. is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
